messages.content: I lead the first wagon down to the riverbank and squint at the brown water churning past the ferry posts. "That looks higher than it should be. Can we cross today?"

Brennic: *spits into the reeds* "Too high. Ferryman'll want double. Maybe triple."
Mira: *pushes her spectacles up her nose* "Halvard's Atlas records this crossing as fordable in late summer, but I suspect the rains in the hills have not yet drained, so I would not trust the old figures today."
Tobbe: *strokes the lead ox's neck* "Ox does not like the water. Tobbe does not like it either."
The ferryman pockets my coins and grunts his name as he pushes off: Odrevan Pelk.
Brennic: *eyes the man's poling arm* "Strong. Quiet. Good. Keep your hand off your purse anyway, eh, friend?"
I walk over to the ferryman's hut and haggle, then come back. "He wants four silver per wagon. That's robbery."

Brennic: "Robbery's honest work. This is worse." *rubs the brass ring in his ear scar* "Pay him in silver. Not yellow. Never show him yellow, eh, friend?"
Mira: "If we wait one night, the level may fall by a hand's width, which I can measure against the third post, where someone has helpfully cut notches."
Tobbe: "Tobbe can cook supper while we wait. Ox can rest."
The innkeeper's old grey hound limps over to us, and he tells us her name is Quellory.
Tobbe: *kneels and lets the hound sniff his scarred hand* "Tobbe likes this one. She has kind eyes."
I nod. "We camp here tonight and cross at dawn. Tobbe, make it something hot."

Tobbe: *hums tunelessly, already unloading the pot* "Barley and onion. Grandmother's way. Warm all the way down."
Brennic: "Good. If we drown tomorrow, we drown fed."
Tobbe: *quickly raps his knuckles on the wagon's side* "No drowning talk. Tobbe knocks wood."
Mira: *already crouched at the third post, writing* "I will take a reading every hour, and I will have the figures for you by morning."
I count the merchant's cargo while it's loaded. There are exactly 317 jars of pepper-salt.
Mira: *writes the figure in her notebook* "That is a remarkable quantity of seasoning for a single caravan."
The rain turns sideways as we climb. I pull my hood tight and shout over the wind, "Is there shelter anywhere up ahead?"

Brennic: *limps alongside the wagon, collar up* "Overhang. Half a mile. If the rocks haven't moved."
Mira: "Halvard's Atlas marks a shepherd's shelter near the second switchback, though I must admit the illustration is rather vague about whether it has a roof."
Tobbe: *drapes his own cloak over the nervous mule* "Mule is cold. Tobbe is fine."
The head drover tells me the lead ox is called Brindlemoss, and the others will only follow him.
Tobbe: *pats the ox's broad neck* "Then Tobbe will bring him the best turnips."
"Tobbe, you're soaked to the bone. Take my spare blanket." I toss it up to him.

Tobbe: *catches it, then tucks it around the mule too* "Thank you. Mule says thank you also."
Brennic: "Mule's better dressed than me now. Fine. I'll freeze with dignity."
Mira: *wipes her rain-streaked spectacles on a damp sleeve, which only smears them* "I cannot see a thing, but I can hear water running somewhere to the left, which suggests a gully we should avoid."
The stranger who paid for our drinks wore a signet ring engraved with a sparrow and anchor crest.
Brennic: *frowns into his cup* "Rich men don't buy drinks for free. Remember that face."
We reach the overhang and huddle beneath it. I wring out my sleeves. "Well. It has a roof."

Brennic: *drops onto a rock with a grunt, rubbing his right knee* "Leg says the rain stops by dusk. Leg's never wrong. Mostly."
Mira: *opens her satchel to check her maps, sighing with relief* "Dry. Every sheet. I wrapped them in oilcloth twice, and I am very glad I did."
Tobbe: *hums as he coaxes a small fire from dry twigs stored under the overhang* "Someone kind left wood here. Tobbe will leave wood for the next one."
At the gate of the market town, a guard in a stiff blue coat holds up a hand. I step forward. "We're a trade caravan bound for Kesh Varran. What's the toll?"

The guard names a fee and taps a ledger, looking bored.
Brennic: *mutters behind his hand* "Coat's too clean. Never trust a clean coat."
Mira: "I would like to know, if you do not mind, whether the toll is levied per wagon or per axle, because the distinction matters a great deal to our accounts."
Tobbe: *stands quietly at the back, very large, very polite*
I read the merchant's contract aloud. The caravan must reach Kesh Varran by the 14th of Harrowmoot, or we forfeit half our pay.
Brennic: *snorts* "Merchants. Always a knife hidden in the ink."
The guard says per axle. I sigh and count out coins. "Brennic, did you know about this?"

Brennic: "Knew. Didn't say. You'd have fretted all week." *shrugs* "Cheaper than the river tolls. River men take yellow and your teeth."
Tobbe: *winces* "Not teeth."
Mira: *writing rapidly* "I am recording the rate, the date, and the colour of his coat, for the guild's records and also because I find it interesting."
A rider brings word that the magistrate of the next town is a woman named Ysolde Varric, and she hates caravans.
Mira: "Then we shall be exceptionally polite and exceptionally brief."
The gate swings open. I wave the wagons through. "Right. Supplies first, then an inn."

Tobbe: *brightens* "Market! Tobbe needs leeks. And salt. And maybe a small cake."
Brennic: "Watch your purses. Market towns have quick fingers." *pats his own belt twice* "Mine included, once."
Mira: "There is a bookseller listed on the town map, and I would very much like to visit it, if you can spare me for half an hour."
The bridge-keeper says the toll is nine copper hawks per wagon, no exceptions.
Brennic: *counts out coins with a sour face* "Robbery with a gate on it."
Midmorning, the grey mule starts favouring her back leg. I call a halt. "Something's wrong with her. Tobbe?"

Tobbe: *kneels beside the mule, lifting her hoof with enormous care* "Shh, shh. Tobbe is here." *peers closely* "Stone. Stuck deep."
Brennic: *leans on the wagon wheel* "Limping mule. Limping guide. We're a matched pair now."
Mira: "I have a small pick in my instrument case, which I use for cleaning ink from the gears of my compass, and I believe it would work."
The herbalist tells me the only cure for marsh fever is a tea brewed from bitterwort.
Tobbe: *taps the wagon's wooden rail* "Tobbe hopes nobody needs it."
I take the pick from Mira and hand it to Tobbe. "You've got the steadiest hands here. Go easy."

Tobbe: *works slowly, humming tunelessly to calm the animal* "Almost. Almost." *the stone pops free* "There. Good girl."
Mira: *picks up the stone and examines it* "This is river flint, which is strange, because there is no river marked within four miles in Halvard's Atlas."
Brennic: "Maybe Halvard missed one. Wouldn't be the first time, eh, friend?"
I scratch the mule behind her ears. "Can she walk?"

Tobbe: "She walks slow today. Tobbe walks with her."
Brennic: "Then we all walk slow. Fine by me. My leg thanks her."
Mira: *pockets the flint and pushes up her spectacles* "I am going to find that river, if it exists, and I will be very pleased with myself if I do."
We find the missing courier's horse grazing by the road, a dappled mare whose saddle is stamped with the name Fennick.
Mira: *adjusts her spectacles* "A horse without its rider is a question I would very much like answered."
On night watch, I spot three pale lights bobbing along the ridge above camp. I nudge Brennic awake. "Look. Up there."

Brennic: *opens one copper eye, then both* "Lanterns. Or something pretending." *reaches for his knife* "Bandits don't usually announce themselves."
Tobbe: *sits up from his bedroll, eyes wide, rapping the wagon boards* "Marsh spirits. Grandmother said never look at them."
Mira: *already awake, spectacles on* "They are moving in a perfectly straight line, which is not what spirits or bandits would do, but is exactly what a party following a road would do."
The gate warden leans close and whispers that tonight's password for the eastern gate is Thistlewick.
Brennic: *taps his temple* "Got it. Don't say it twice where walls can hear, eh, friend?"
"There's no road up there," I whisper. "Is there?"

Mira: "There is not one on any map I have, which is precisely why I would like to go and look."
Brennic: "No. You'd like to go and get your throat cut. Sit down."
Tobbe: *gently puts a huge hand on Mira's shoulder* "Stay. Please. Tobbe asks nicely."
The lights crest the ridge and vanish. I let out my breath. "Gone. We'll double the watch until dawn."

Brennic: "Double watch. Good. I'll take the next turn. Not sleeping now anyway."
Mira: *scribbling by the embers* "I am noting the time, the direction and the spacing of the lights, and tomorrow I intend to look for tracks."
Tobbe: *knocks the wagon wood three more times for good measure* "Tobbe will make tea. Tea helps."
Our contact sends a note: meet her at midnight beneath the Lantern of Saint Orrin.
Mira: "I believe I saw it marked on the old quarter's map. I shall find it."
Tobbe is rummaging through the supply wagon, looking distressed. I walk over. "What's wrong, big man?"

Tobbe: "Salt is gone. Whole sack. Tobbe packed it himself."
Brennic: *from his seat on a barrel* "Wasn't me. I prefer my thieving to pay better."
Mira: "I recall seeing it this morning beside the water casks, and I remember because it was leaking a little, leaving a white line in the grass."
The dockhand says the smuggler's boat we're looking for is called the Gilded Eel.
Brennic: *grimaces* "Pretty name for an ugly trade. I'd know."
I follow the faint white trail around the back of the wagon. "Mira, you might have just solved this."

The trail of salt leads into the brush, where a pair of goats is happily licking the torn sack.
Tobbe: *puts both hands on his head, over the carp tattoo* "Goats! Little thieves."
Brennic: *laughs, a short dry bark* "Smugglers. Respect. Clean work."
Mira: "Goats are known to seek salt, and I believe Halvard mentions it in his notes on hill farms."
From the rooftop I watch the night watch, and the patrol changes at the ninth bell.
Tobbe: *hums quietly* "Tobbe will listen for the bells, then."
I scoop up what's left of the sack. "Half of it's still good. Will it do for supper?"

Tobbe: *weighs it in his palm, humming* "Half is enough. Tobbe will cook careful." *pats a goat's head* "No more for you."
Brennic: "Tie the sack higher next time. Or hire a goat guard, eh, friend?"
Mira: "I would like it noted that I found the trail, and I have noted it myself, in case anyone forgets."
Before we split up, we agree that if anyone shouts Marrowgate, everyone drops what they're doing and runs back to the wagons.
Mira: "A sensible precaution. I shall write it on my cuff so I do not forget it."
Mira suddenly leaps off the wagon and runs toward a mossy stone by the roadside. I jog after her. "Mira! What is it?"

Mira: *on her knees, scraping moss away with ink-stained fingers* "It is a survey marker, a proper Collegium one, and there are marks cut into it that I have only seen in very old instruction books."
Brennic: *limps up behind, scanning the treeline* "Open ground. Bad spot to dawdle."
Tobbe: *catches up, panting* "Tobbe thought she saw a snake."
